name: GitHub
approach: A README with a working quickstart, an example project and release notes, so the first visit can end in a successful install or run
measure: Stars as a weak interest signal, 14-day traffic (views, unique visitors, clones, referrers) collected weekly, and downstream installs or use from your own analytics
risk: Stars measure appreciation, can be removed and can come from curiosity; traffic history is only 14 days and needs write access; buying stars or automated starring breaks GitHub's rules
complexity: Low; public metrics need no token, traffic needs a token for a repository you can push to
maintainability: Keep the quickstart tested and collect traffic at least every 14 days, since older days are lost

name: Show HN
approach: A substantive project people can try without signing up, a plain maker explanation, and thoughtful replies from someone present in the thread
measure: Thread comments read for objections and questions, tagged product activation, with points kept as a weak attention signal
risk: Points are not readers and some votes are dropped by anti-abuse software; asking friends to vote, signup-gated pages and quick one-offs break the guidelines and can bury the post
complexity: Low setup; timing, ranking and discussion tone are unpredictable and flags can end a post
maintainability: Be available to answer for the first hours; no routine version-bump posts and no delete-and-resubmit

name: YouTube
approach: Show the payoff or a useful tutorial with a directly tryable next step, with the audience setting decided before upload
measure: Views and impressions click-through rate as exposure, then tagged visits, successful first use and return
risk: Public playback starts can look impressive without product interest; mislabelling the audience setting or misleading titles and thumbnails can bring restrictions or strikes
complexity: Moderate production; metric definitions, reporting delay and the made-for-kids decision all matter
maintainability: Batch footage; keep one reusable demonstration format; re-check YouTube's metric definitions, which have changed

name: TikTok
approach: Show the real payoff in the first seconds as a short vertical video, with one tryable next step in the profile link or caption
measure: Video views at 100% and average play time by video length, tagged profile-link visits, first use and return
risk: Views measure attention, not first use or payment; promotional posts need the content disclosure setting; engagement tricks and bulk automation break integrity rules
complexity: Moderate: vertical production and in-app analytics that differ from the ads-side definitions
maintainability: Batch clips from real play or use; no automation, bought engagement or reposting bots

name: Facebook Groups and Pages
cost: 0 for organic posts; ads are separate spend
approach: Share one tryable link in a relevant Group under its rules, or on your own Page, and disclose any commercial relationship
measure: Tagged link visits, replies and objections, first use and return, with Page impressions or Views kept as exposure only
risk: Exposure counts overstate interest; Group promotion rules vary; very high-frequency posting, bought engagement and misleading links break the spam rules
complexity: Moderate: Group-by-Group judgment, and Meta renames and redefines its metrics
maintainability: Show up as a participant, not a poster; re-check metric names when exporting

name: X
cost: 0 for organic posts; API access and ads are separate spend
approach: Post a short demonstration with one tryable link, reply by hand to people who respond, and join an existing builder or genre conversation
measure: Replies and objections, tagged link visits, first use and return, with post impressions kept as exposure only
risk: Impressions are not unique people and say nothing about use; bulk or unsolicited replies, engagement schemes and unlabelled bots break the rules; API terms and pricing change
complexity: Low to post by hand; high if automated, because automation needs labels, consent and prior approval for some uses
maintainability: Do it by hand; no reply, like or follow automation; re-read the rules before any API use

name: Steam store page and wishlists
cost: $100 per app, recoupable after $1,000 adjusted gross revenue, plus production effort; verify current terms
approach: Publish a coming-soon page early, send tagged traffic from your other channels to it, and read wishlist additions and tracked visits per source
measure: Wishlist additions net of deletions, UTM tracked visits and wishlist conversions by source, later wishlist purchases
risk: A wishlist is intent, not payment; tracked visits only count signed-in users so they are a lower bound; there is a 30-day wait after paying the fee and a two-week minimum coming-soon period
complexity: Moderate to high: store page assets, Steamworks setup, bank and tax verification, and a review before the page goes live
maintainability: Check reports daily around launches; tag every outbound link; Valve's rules and fees change, so re-read them before committing

name: Instagram
cost: 0 for organic posts; ads and creator fees are separate spend
approach: Post one short, honest piece of work with a tagged link in the bio or caption, disclose any paid partner, and read accounts reached and tagged visits
measure: Tagged link visits, comments and saves read by hand, first use and return, with Plays and Accounts reached kept as exposure only
risk: Exposure counts overstate interest; Meta renames and redefines Instagram metrics; bought engagement, automation and undisclosed paid partnerships break the rules; teen audiences need extra care
complexity: Moderate: visual production each post, and Meta's metric names and partnership tools change
maintainability: Re-check the in-app (i) metric definitions before each export; keep disclosure and tagging habits the same every post

name: Twitch
cost: 0 to stream; production time and any ads are separate
approach: Go live on a schedule with the project as the subject, take part in the chat as a person, and send viewers to one tagged link
measure: Average viewers, unique viewers, follows and minutes watched from Twitch analytics, plus tagged link visits and first use from your own analytics
risk: Small channels get few viewers; artificial viewers or follows break the rules; viewers must be 13 or older and minors need supervision
complexity: Moderate: streaming setup, schedule and live moderation
maintainability: Needs steady live hours; Twitch redesigns its analytics, so re-check metric names before comparing weeks

name: Bluesky
cost: 0 for organic posts; API use is rate limited, not priced, in the pages read
approach: Post as a person, share one tryable link with context, and build or follow a feed or bot only if it self-labels and acts on request
measure: Tagged link visits, replies and objections read by hand, first use and return from your own analytics
risk: Small reach is unproven; artificially manipulating social signals and unlabelled or unwanted bot replies break the rules; no first-party analytics found in the pages read
complexity: Low for posting, moderate for bots or feeds because of rate limits and labelling
maintainability: Guidelines and API limits change; re-read them before running anything automated

name: Apple App Store
cost: $99 per year for the Apple Developer Program (USD, may vary by region), plus production effort; accredited educational institutions can apply for a fee waiver; verify current terms
approach: Ship an accurate listing, send tagged traffic from your other channels to the product page through campaign links, and read product page views, downloads and conversion by source type and campaign
measure: Unique impressions, unique product page views, total and first-time downloads and conversion rate by source type and campaign link, later your own analytics for use and return
risk: Listings that mislead, manipulate reviews or rankings, or use kids terms outside the Kids Category can be removed and the developer expelled; metrics appear only above small thresholds and downloads are not use
complexity: Moderate: Developer Program enrollment, App Store Connect setup, a build and listing that pass App Review, plus extra constraints if an app is aimed at children
maintainability: Check App Analytics weekly around releases; make a new campaign link per outbound source; Apple's guidelines and fees change, so re-read them before each submission

name: Google Play
cost: $25 one-time Play Console registration fee, plus production effort; verify current terms
approach: Publish an accurate store listing, send UTM-tagged traffic from your other channels to it, and read store listing visitors, first-time installers and tracked channels in Play Console
measure: Store listing visitors, first-time installers and conversion between segments, with UTM-tagged channels shown separately from untagged third-party referrers
risk: Incentivized or fraudulent ratings, reviews and installs breach policy; apps whose audience includes children must meet the Families requirements; new personal accounts have testing and device checks before release; installs are not use
complexity: Moderate: account identity verification, a signed build, listing, target-audience and content declarations, and a policy review; higher if children are in the target audience
maintainability: Check Play Console statistics weekly around releases; tag every outbound link; policies and report labels change, so re-read them before each release

name: Relevant Reddit communities
approach: Inspect community rules; contribute a useful native explanation where promotion is welcome, and ask for objections before asking for visits
measure: Objections, tagged use and return from the specific community, with votes and comments read by hand
risk: Repetitive promotion can be spam; no blanket posting allowance; some communities ban self-promotion outright; accounts can be banned
maintainability: Build relationships; do not run a promotional bot; re-read each community's rules before each post

name: itch.io and game communities
approach: Playable demo, genre-readable screenshots and a brief development log, with each outside link tagged so itch.io referrers and your own analytics can be compared
measure: Page views, downloads or browser plays, purchases and the referrer for each; qualified plays, completion and returning players only from the game's own telemetry
risk: Audience and device fit may differ from your intended players; itch.io reports file delivery and referrals, not how the game is played; a download counts as started, not finished
complexity: Moderate asset preparation and distribution setup
maintainability: Maintain the playable build and respond to bug reports; never sign people up to a mailing list automatically

name: Search and useful documentation
approach: Answer a real recurring question with a useful page and a working example, then read Search Console for the queries that show it
measure: Search Console clicks and impressions by query and page, then qualified visits and successful use from your own analytics
risk: Slow feedback, from hours to several months; ranking is not guaranteed; mass-produced or manipulative pages can be demoted or removed
complexity: Instrumentation, indexable pages, Search Console setup and topic judgment
maintainability: Update examples and monitor query intent; avoid scaled or doorway pages

name: Opt-in email
approach: Useful update to people who opted in, with accurate sender details, a working unsubscribe and one clear next action
measure: Tagged successful use and unsubscribes; treat opens cautiously because mail privacy features can load tracking images without a person reading
risk: A small list limits discovery; unwanted mail harms trust and, at volume, spam complaints above provider thresholds cause blocked delivery; breaking consent or opt-out rules brings legal penalties
complexity: Consent, list care, sender authentication and deliverability
maintainability: Keep the cadence sustainable; honour unsubscribes quickly and keep a suppression list; recheck provider and legal rules, which change

name: Existing Discord community
approach: Share useful progress and invite focused feedback in a relevant existing community, as a person and with the server's permission
measure: Playtest participation, recurring use and qualitative themes, counted from your own tagged links and notes; Server Insights only where your own server qualifies
risk: Starting a new empty server creates moderation work before demand; unsolicited bulk messages, self-bots and bought or inflated engagement break Discord's rules and can end the account
maintainability: Only open your own community when you can sustain it; follow each server's rules on self-promotion

name: LinkedIn
approach: Concrete before/after workflow for the professional audience, shared as a post or in answer to a real question, with one tryable link
measure: Qualified conversations, tagged link visits and product use, with post impressions kept as exposure only
risk: Impressions and generic praise are weak demand signals; promotional invitations to strangers, repetitive messages and automation tools break the rules and can restrict the account
complexity: Requires clear professional relevance and a credible demo; analytics definitions differ between LinkedIn's own pages
maintainability: Reuse actual user stories with permission; no scraping, extensions or outreach automation

name: Product Hunt
cost: 0 for a basic launch; verify current terms
approach: A prepared maker launch from a personal account: short tagline, two or more gallery images, a first comment asking for feedback, and a maker available to answer all day
measure: Visits arriving from Product Hunt in your own analytics, activation, and the content of comments; votes and rank are recorded by hand as context
risk: Launch-day rank rests on upvotes, comments and undisclosed factors and is not durable demand; asking for upvotes, paying for traffic or upvote contests can remove the post
complexity: Moderate preparation; the submission link cannot be a tracking link, so attribution relies on referrers
maintainability: Plan support and a follow-up beyond launch day; check the live launch guide before each launch
